newsitem.title: GERMANY: German upper house votes to move to Berlin.
newsitem.headline: German upper house votes to move to Berlin.

text.p: Germany's upper house of parliament, the Bundesrat, voted on Friday to move to Berlin by the end of the century when the government and lower house also move to the capital of unified Germany.
Thirteen of Germany's 16 regional states represented in the Bundesrat backed the proposal to move to Berlin later this decade reversing their decision five years ago to stay in Bonn.

Bundesrat members have complained that the upper house would lose influence if it were to stay behind in Bonn, while the 672-member lower house moved to the seat of government in Berlin of Berlin, 600 km (375 miles) to the east.
Many argue it would also be a waste of money if officials had to shuttle between the two legislative chambers hundreds of miles (km) apart.

Even Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who has supported efforts to keep some federal ministries in Bonn, had called the Bundesrat's 1991 decision to stay behind after the rest of the government moves to Berlin absurd.
The government plans to move from Bonn, a quiet Rhineside town of 300,000 that was West Germany's provisional capital between 1949 and 1990, to the 3.4 million city in 1999.
